questions.explanation: Every call puts its own element in front of the string the rest of the array produces, so the order follows the index upward as 2, then 5, then 7, and the base case adds only an empty string, leaving the space that 7 already emitted. The reverse answer in B is the belief that returning from recursion unwinds the elements too, when in fact each frame only prefixes a finished string.
questions.hint: Decide whether a frame prefixes or appends the rest of the list.
questions.learningObjective: trace list building by string concatenation

"7 5 2 " with a trailing space
options.misconception: believes recursion yields the elements in reverse

options.text: "2 5 7" with no trailing space
options.misconception: believes the base case contributes no space

options.text: " 2 5 7" preceded by one space
options.misconception: believes concatenation evaluates right to left

questions.explanation: Each call halves the argument, and 100 walks 100, 50, 25, 12, 6, 3, 1, 0, which is 8 invocations including the base case. The set-bit count of 3 is what the method returns rather than what it costs, so 4 in C is the belief that the answer bounds the work, and the call on 0 is a real frame, which is why the chain is one longer than the halvings alone.
questions.hint: Halve until you reach 0 and count every value you passed.
questions.learningObjective: count invocations of a halving method on 100

options.text: 7, because the call on 0 is only a base case
options.misconception: believes the terminating call is not counted

options.text: 4, because 100 in binary has four set bits
options.misconception: confuses the returned count with the call count

options.text: 9, because each of the 7 steps also calls a helper
options.misconception: believes the modulus triggers a second call

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING

questions.explanation: The first call peels a, so every a and b character comes out before the digits, then b's character prints and the call recurses on the unpeeled a again, which is why 1, 2, 1, 2, 2 follow the letters. When one string empties, the base case dumps whatever is left of the other, and neither base case trims it, so 18 characters emerge. Swapping the print order in B reverses the whole line, which is the belief that a print before a call still waits for it.
questions.hint: Expand one call at a time, listing both recursive calls in order.
questions.learningObjective: expand a method that recurses twice per call

options.misconception: believes the a character prints after its own call

options.text: prints "aaab2ab1aab2ab"
options.misconception: believes the first call should consume from b

options.misconception: believes the second call should consume from both
